long_biography.plain_text:
Filmmaker Tom Jones rebuilt his Asbury Park documentary after Bruce Springsteen agreed to an interview. The musician's recollections allowed Jones to restore material he had previously cut. He also added concert footage that brought established performers together with young local musicians, giving the revised film a connection to the city's new generation.

For The Real Deal, Jones directed and co-wrote a documentary with John Malpede about the Los Angeles Poverty Department. Filming performances and street life, they followed a theatre company made up primarily of homeless people. Jones combined excerpts from two decades of performances with interviews with former participants, local officials and the group's supporters.
